chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
When you are behind an Imam whom you follow, then be silent and glorify (God) within yourself.

key_terms.تَأْتَمُّ بِهِ: To follow him (as a follower in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a follower do with their recitation and glorification when praying behind an Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'listening' (istima') for the follower during the Imam's recitation, a key distinction in Shia fiqh that differentiates the ma'mum's role from the Imam's. It emphasizes internal devotion (tasbih bil-qalb) to maintain the solemnity of the prayer, reflecting the scholarly consensus on the etiquette of following the leader in congregational worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘When you were to be behind a Imam, complete with him, and be silent (during the recitation), and Glorify within yourself’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If you perform Salah (prayer) behind an Imam whom you follow then remain silent and say Tasbih (Allah is free of all defects) to yourself only.’”
